title: How to Choose the Best Interior Door for Your Space
content_html:
How to Choose the Best Interior Door for Your Space

Interior doors do far more than separate rooms. The right door can completely change the look and feel of a home, adding warmth, character, elegance, and architectural style. Whether your design leans modern, traditional, farmhouse, or transitional, interior doors are one of the most important decorative elements in a home — not just a functional necessity.

At The Royal Wood Shop, homeowners and contractors can find interior doors in virtually every size and style, with excellent pricing and a large in-stock selection ready for renovation and new construction projects.

Why Interior Doors Matter

Interior doors are used throughout every room in your home, so consistency in style can dramatically improve the overall design flow. Clean modern doors can create a sleek contemporary feel, while classic panel doors add depth and timeless character. Because doors are repeated throughout the entire home, they become a major visual feature that ties everything together.

The best interior door choice depends on:

  • Your home’s architectural style
  • Whether the door will be painted or stained
  • Your budget
  • Sound control requirements
  • Durability needs
  • Desired level of design detail

Popular Interior Door Styles

Shaker Doors

Shaker doors are one of the most popular interior door styles today because of their clean lines and timeless appearance. Their simple recessed panel design works beautifully in modern, transitional, Scandinavian, farmhouse, and even traditional homes.

Benefits of shaker doors include:

  • Clean, minimalist appearance
  • Timeless style that won’t quickly date
  • Easy to coordinate with modern trim and cabinetry
  • Available in 1-panel, 2-panel, 3-panel, and 5-panel configurations
  • Excellent for both painted and stained finishes

Single-panel shaker doors often suit contemporary spaces, while multi-panel designs add a more traditional architectural look.

Molded Panel Doors

Molded panel doors remain one of the most affordable and practical interior door options available. These doors are manufactured using molded wood composite materials and are available in countless styles, from traditional raised panels to modern shaker profiles.

Advantages of molded panel doors include:

  • Budget-friendly pricing
  • Consistent smooth finish
  • Resistant to shrinking and cracking
  • Lightweight options available
  • Excellent painted appearance

Molded doors are commonly available in:

  • Hollow core construction
  • Solid core construction
  • Smooth finishes
  • Woodgrain textured finishes

For many homeowners, molded panel doors offer the best balance between appearance and affordability.

Stain Grade Wood Doors

Nothing matches the warmth and richness of real wood grain. Stain grade doors showcase the natural beauty of wood species like oak, maple, walnut, and mahogany, making them a premium choice for upscale interiors.

Stain grade wood doors are ideal for:

  • Luxury homes
  • Rustic and farmhouse interiors
  • Traditional architecture
  • Natural wood trim packages
  • Spaces where warmth and texture are desired

Unlike painted doors, stain grade doors highlight natural grain patterns and unique wood character. Every door becomes slightly unique, adding authenticity and craftsmanship to the home.

Understanding Door Construction Types

Choosing the right construction type is just as important as selecting the style.

Hollow Core Doors

Hollow core doors are the most economical option. They are lightweight and ideal for closets, pantries, and low-traffic areas.

Best for:

  • Budget-conscious projects
  • Closets and utility rooms
  • Basic residential applications

Solid Core Doors

Solid core doors are heavier, quieter, and feel more substantial. They provide significantly better sound reduction between rooms and offer a more premium feel throughout the home.

Best for:

  • Bedrooms
  • Bathrooms
  • Home offices
  • Higher-end renovations
  • Noise reduction

Solid Wood Doors

Solid wood doors are the premium option, valued for their beauty, durability, and authentic craftsmanship. These doors are typically used in luxury homes or stain-grade applications.

Best for:

  • Custom homes
  • High-end interiors
  • Stained finishes
  • Traditional craftsmanship

Interior Door Cost Considerations

Interior door pricing varies significantly depending on style, material, and construction.

Budget-Friendly Options

  • Hollow core molded doors
  • Basic smooth panel designs
  • Primed paint-grade finishes

Mid-Range Options

  • Solid core molded doors
  • Shaker style doors
  • MDF and engineered wood construction

Premium Options

  • Solid wood doors
  • Stain grade hardwood doors
  • Custom sizes and profiles
  • Specialty veneers and finishes

While premium doors cost more upfront, they often add noticeable value and visual impact throughout the home.

Painted vs. Stained Doors

Painted doors remain extremely popular because they create a clean, bright, consistent appearance. White shaker doors especially continue to dominate modern interior design trends.

Stained doors offer a warmer, more natural aesthetic that highlights real wood grain and texture. These finishes pair beautifully with hardwood flooring, exposed beams, and natural trim details.

Choosing the Right Door for Your Home

Here are a few general recommendations:

  • Modern homes: Single-panel shaker or flush doors
  • Transitional homes: 2-panel or 3-panel shaker doors
  • Traditional homes: Raised panel wood doors
  • Farmhouse interiors: Shaker stain-grade wood doors
  • Budget renovations: Molded panel doors
  • Luxury spaces: Solid core or solid wood stain-grade doors

The key is maintaining consistency throughout the home so every room feels connected.

title: Poplar vs MDF Trim in Toronto & the GTA: Cost, Quality & Best Applications
content_html:
When selecting interior trim, baseboards, casing, or mouldings in Toronto and the GTA, one of the most common decisions contractors and homeowners face is choosing between Poplar wood and MDF (Medium Density Fibreboard).

At Royal Wood Shop, we stock both options in a wide range of trim profiles, primed mouldings, baseboards, casing, and custom millwork solutions, helping builders, renovators, and designers across Ontario find the right balance of cost, durability, and finish quality.

Cost vs Quality: What Really Matters in Toronto Trim Projects

On paper, there can appear to be a noticeable price difference between Poplar trim and MDF mouldings in the GTA market. However, once you factor in:

  • Installation labour
  • Sanding, Priming and painting Labour

In many Toronto renovation and new build projects, labour is the largest expense and the real cost gap becomes smaller if you are hiring professionals to install and paint.

MDF in the Modern Construction Industry (Toronto & Ontario Trend)

Over the last decade, MDF trim and MDF mouldings in Ontario have become widely accepted across the construction industry.

What was once considered a budget alternative is now commonly used in:

  • Custom homes across the GTA
  • Condominium developments in Toronto
  • Commercial millwork and retail interiors
  • Kitchen cabinet manufacturing

In fact, the cabinet industry has fully embraced MDF doors, especially for painted finishes. Even high-end cabinet makers now prefer MDF for:

  • CNC precision machining
  • Smooth painted finishes
  • Consistent, defect-free surfaces

This same logic now applies to interior trim and baseboards in Toronto homes.

When to Use Poplar or MDF for Interior Trim

At Royal Wood Shop, we recommend both Poplar and MDF depending on the application. Each performs extremely well when properly installed and painted.

Both materials are widely used across:

  • Baseboards
  • Door and window casing
  • Crown moulding
  • Wainscoting and wall paneling
  • Custom millwork packages

Poplar Trim (Finger-Joint & Solid Options) – Pros & Benefits

Poplar remains one of the most trusted choices for paint-grade trim in the GTA market.

Key Advantages of Poplar:

  • Harder and more durable than MDF
  • Lighter weight and easier to handle on-site
  • Excellent for high-traffic areas in Toronto homes
  • Deeper, sharper profile details for a more premium look
  • Nail holes fill cleanly for smooth finishing results
  • Available in primed finger-joint Poplar profiles in stock
  • Custom profiles available with fast lead times
  • Manufactured in Ontario through established millwork production (Alexandria / Royal Woodworking supply chain)

Poplar is often preferred by professional trim carpenters in Toronto and York Region who want long-term durability and traditional wood performance.

MDF Trim & Mouldings – Pros & Benefits

MDF has become one of the most popular choices for modern painted trim in Toronto and the GTA due to its consistency and affordability.

Key Advantages of MDF:

  • Perfectly consistent milling with no knots or natural defects
  • Factory primed and ready for paint
  • Extremely stable—does not warp or twist
  • Ideal for long straight runs of baseboard and casing
  • More cost-effective than solid wood alternatives
  • Perfect for modern minimalist and contemporary interiors
  • CNC-friendly for precision millwork applications
  • Commonly used in cabinetry and architectural millwork
  • Phase 2 California compliant and formaldehyde-safe materials

For most Toronto contractors and renovation companies, MDF offers the fastest, cleanest installation for painted interiors and they firmly maintain that durability over time is very good with MDF.

Protecting MDF Baseboard in GTA Homes

While MDF performs extremely well indoors, it is softer than wood and can be vulnerable to impact damage in high-traffic areas, especially baseboard on outside corners.

To improve longevity, we recommend:

  • Installing a wood shoe moulding or quarter round at the base of MDF baseboards
  • Using wood trim at floor level in high-impact zones
  • Adding backband moulding in Poplar or wood for door and window casings to protect MDF edges
  • Avoiding direct moisture exposure from mops or cleaning equipment

These simple upgrades significantly extend the life of MDF trim installations in Toronto homes and condos.

How to Repair Damaged MDF Baseboard and Trim

MDF trim is easy to repair when minor dents or chips occur.

Basic Repair Process:

  1. Clean and remove loose debris with sandpaper
  2. Seal damaged area with primer
  3. Apply wood filler or patch compound
  4. Shape and sand to match original profile
  5. Re-prime and apply final paint coat

With proper finishing, repaired MDF blends seamlessly into existing trimwork.

Why Contractors in Toronto Choose Royal Wood Shop

At Royal Wood Shop, we supply premium interior trim, baseboards, casing, mouldings, and millwork products across Toronto, York Region, and the GTA.

We stock:

  • Poplar baseboards and casing (primed finger-joint options)
  • MDF trim boards and moulding profiles
  • Modern, traditional, and transitional profiles
  • Custom millwork solutions with fast turnaround

Whether you're a trim carpenter, builder, renovation contractor, or homeowner, our team helps you choose the right material for performance, budget, and design.

Final Summary: Poplar vs MDF in Toronto Interiors

When comparing Poplar vs MDF trim in the GTA market, both materials are excellent choices for painted interiors.

  • Choose Poplar trim in Toronto if you want durability, sharper profiles, and a more traditional wood feel, or a custom non stock profile.
  • Choose MDF mouldings in the GTA if you want cost efficiency, consistency, and ultra-smooth painted finishes

In most modern interior projects across Ontario, both materials perform exceptionally well when installed and finished correctly.
